identity_evidence.quote: A 78-year-old male with a history of hypertension

attribution_limitations: The text states a BMI of 15.7 Kg/m^(2) 22 days after adding the main course, while Table 1 prints 15.2 for the 8th month (March, 2024), and the timeline figure prints 15.2 under its gastric residue marker (pixel content only). The text time is not literally the Table 1 column, so this is recorded as an ambiguity, not a two-sided source conflict: the text value is review_only and the table value stays as printed.

Stated weight changes do not all match differences of Table 1 weights: gains of 3.1 kg (April 2024) and 1.5 kg (May 2024) versus 3.0 kg (45.0 to 48.0) and 1.6 kg (48.0 to 49.6); the total loss of 9.5 kg equals 53.9 to 44.4, not 55.7 to 44.4, and its baseline is not stated. Arithmetic or rounding differences, not source conflicts; all values kept as printed.

Table 1 prints "Normal value <24 cm" for MUAC and "Normal value <31 cm" for calf circumference, while the text calls the admission MUAC of 26.0 cm and CC of 31.5 cm normal and states that values below the 24 cm and 31 cm cutoffs indicate underweight and sarcopenia. The admission flags follow the explicit text; no flag is derived from the printed table labels.
Table 2 prints the February potassium as 4,3 with a decimal comma; kept as text rather than parsed.
The examination lists "pulse flexion" without a body site; the wording is kept as printed and not reinterpreted.
The text says Table 3 compares three diets but the table prints four diet columns (adding the hipercaloric formula). All four printed columns are recorded.

The discussion offers hedged causes for the abnormal results (low urea and creatinine possibly from low muscle mass; elevated CRP possibly from vascular epilepsy or post-stroke inflammation; single elevated glucose and low potassium values without conclusions). The high/low flags are recorded only where the text classifies a specific result (abnormal at admission, abnormal glucose in February, abnormal values at the last assessment) with the printed interval; the hedged causes are not recorded as asserted causes.

The abstract and discussion report improved biochemical parameters and muscle mass, but Table 2 shows mixed laboratory changes (for example C-reactive protein 2.09, 0.34 then 2.53 mg/dL) and muscle mass is not measured; the abstract claim is kept review_only.

The PEG paragraph says the PEG was placed to address existing malnutrition and sarcopenia, while the discussion says the patient was not yet classified as sarcopenic at the first two calf measurements and sarcopenia was confirmed only at the third (February, 2024). Sarcopenia is not dated to the PEG placement.
Chronic inflammation post-stroke is named only as the GLIM etiological criterion for malnutrition; it is not recorded as a separate diagnosed condition.
Text BMI values 18.2, 15.0 and 16.2 match Table 1 cells but their own sentences state no time, so they are kept as separate untimed items rather than merged with the table cells.

claims.text: One month after admission chronic bronchitis was diagnosed with dyspnea, wheezing and productive cough, and a PEG was placed to improve nutritional status while keeping the homemade liquid diet. A multidisciplinary team chose the PEG over the nasogastric tube for long-term feeding. Calf circumference fell below 31 cm by February 2024, confirming sarcopenia, and the authors classified moderate malnutrition and mild anemia.

evidence.quote: One month after nursing home admission (September, 2023), a chronic bronchitis was diagnosed and symptoms such as, dyspnea, wheezing and productive cough were observed.
A PEG was placed to improve the patient’s nutritional status while maintaining the HLD.

The decision to place the PEG over the nasogastric tube (NGT), which was present at admission, was made by a multidisciplinary team and considered the specific case, clinical situation, diagnosis, prognosis, ethical factors, and the family’s wishes.
The primary goals were to prevent further weight loss, correct nutritional deficiencies, and enhance the patient’s quality of life related to inadequate oral intake
The choice of PEG placement rather than continue with the NGT was based on the NGT’s suitability for only short-term use (up to 4–6 weeks).
in the third measurement (February, 2024), the CC value was <31 cm, which confirmed a diagnosis of sarcopenia
According to the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) criteria, the patient is malnourished since he has 1 phenotypic criterion and 1 etiological criterion for malnutrition diagnosis
it was possible to confirm that the patient was in stage 1 of malnutrition (moderate malnutrition)
because of moderate malnutrition
Throughout follow-up, the patient consistently had hemoglobin and hematocrit values below the reference values. It was also possible to classify the patient’s anemia as mild

claims.text: Six months after PEG placement a normocaloric enteric formula was added to the diet. Weight loss continued, so a main course was added and later removed because of gastric contents before meals and possible gastric stasis. A hypercaloric enteral formula replaced the normocaloric one for 5 days. In April 2024 diarrhea led to stopping the normocaloric formula and an antidiarrheal diet, after which the diet and formula were reintroduced.

evidence.quote: Six months after PEG placement (February, 2024), a normocaloric enteric formula (NEF) was prescribed, as a complement to the HLD to reinforce the patient’s diet which increased the total energy intake by 500 Kcal daily.
The NEF (500 mL per day) was given at breakfast and dinner and the HLD at lunch, afternoon and evening snack.

to increase daily energy intake (an increase of 227 Kcal), it was added the main course at lunch to the HDL. The main course consisted of meat or fish and potatoes, rice or pasta ground in a blender with a small amount of water to make it liquid enough to pass through the PEG.

During the following month (April 2024), several episodes of diarrhea occurred, leading to the discontinuation of NEF and implementation of an antidiarrheal diet.
The anti-diarrhea diet excludes greens, dairy products and only uses fat-free cooking methods such as grilling and boiling.
By the end of month and after recovering diarrhea episodes (normal feces), the patient showed good tolerance to the reintroduction of HLD and the NEF supplementation.

Six months after PEG placement (February, 2024), a normocaloric enteric formula (NEF) was prescribed, as a complement to the HLD to reinforce the patient’s diet which increased the total energy intake by 500 Kcal daily.
The NEF (500 mL per day) was given at breakfast and dinner and the HLD at lunch, afternoon and evening snack.
Taken in account that patient still had a low body weight and visibly weakened state, a hypercaloric enteral formula (HEF) was prescribed to replace the NEF for 5 days.
During the following month (April 2024), several episodes of diarrhea occurred, leading to the discontinuation of NEF and implementation of an antidiarrheal diet.
